newsitem.title: GREECE: Mytilineos sees fast growth after deal with Trepca.
newsitem.headline: Mytilineos sees fast growth after deal with Trepca.

text.p: Metals trading firm Mytilineos will raise its 1996 dividend per share to 50 drachmas from 28 a year earlier and expects substantial growth in turnover and profit after clinching a deal with Trepca Mines.
Turnover in 1997 is expected to rise to 43 billion drachmas with pretax earnings growing to 2.17 billion, a conservative projection, board chairman Evangelos Mytilineos told reporters on Tuesday.
The company posted turnover of 17 billion in 1995 and pretax profit of 717 million drachmas.
Mytilineos signed a major five-year $517 million deal with RMHK Trepca Mines in rump Yugoslavia on Monday to modernise its mines and distribute its final product to international markets.
In the first four months of the year it has realised turnover of 14.5 billion and pretax profit of 725 million drachmas.

The deal will be financed by retained earnings and open credit line facilities of 25 billion drachmas. A rights issue is also in the works some time in the second half of 1997 but no further details were disclosed.
"We had promised shareholders that we would seek to raise additional equity once our international investment activities enter a more permanent stage," Mytilineos said.

The recent deal with Trepca complements a similar agreement with Sasha Mines in FYROM and will play a crucial role in the recovery of the Serbian mining industry which needs to keep exports going, he said.
As a result, some 100,000 tonnes of lead and zinc annually will be sold in central and eastern European markets.
Another factor that enabled Mytilineos to clinch the deal was the insurance coverage facility provided by OAEP -- Greece's Export Credit Insurance Organisation.
Mytilineos markets base metals, ores and concentrates, steel and semi-finished products internationally and has grown to the largest player in the Balkan region.
